attribution.note: Both occurrences are Zitron's own words on his newsletter. The August 2024 post restates the prediction and says he stands by it.

semantics.note: 'I believe' plus 'will be... savaging' is an unhedged expectation, and he later calls it 'my prediction'. 'Three quarters to prove itself' frames a deadline rather than a true antecedent. Strictly, the savaging follows the 'apocalypse' at the window's end, so the drafter's 'by end of 2024' is slightly tight, but it is a fair reading.

contract.note: Testing Q4 2024 year-over-year revenue for Microsoft and Alphabet, both named in the post, is fair. A possible lag after the window is a caveat. But double-digit growth at the deadline is the opposite of savaging under any reasonable reading. Amazon is missing, which does not change the result.

evidence.note: Microsoft's own release covers the quarter ended 2024-12-31: revenue $69.6B, up 12% year over year. Available 2025-01-29, before the evaluation date. It is a company disclosure, which is the source the contract requires.
Alphabet's Q4 2024 release (archived copy) reports revenue up 12% year over year to $96.5B. Available 2025-02-04. Revenue growth, not a fall.
Zitron's 2026 admission that he 'goofed' on the three-quarters claim. It is the speaker's own statement and cannot decide the outcome. Context only.

output.rationale: Zitron forecast that AI would face an 'apocalypse' after three quarters from March 2024, savaging big tech revenues. The horizon has elapsed. In the quarter ending 2024-12-31, Microsoft and Alphabet, both named in the post, each reported revenue up 12% year over year. That meets the contract's contradiction condition. Amazon's figures were unavailable, but two of the largest companies growing strongly is incompatible with 'savaging'.
